param.name: reference
param.label: Reference CDS
param.help: In-frame coding sequence (FASTA) of the target gene. Only the first record is used unless stated otherwise.

macros.token:
This tool is part of the **disassembler** suite, which reconstructs in-frame coding haplotypes of a target gene from planetary-scale sequence indexes: `Logan <https://github.com/IndexThePlanet/Logan>`_ unitigs found through a kmindex search, or Logan contigs found through a LexicMap search. Both routes end in a reference-guided codon alignment and a phylogeny.
The kmindex route runs **harvest** (merge the kmindex query shards), **stratify** (optional: cut a size-capped cohort), **walker** (reconstruct one haplotype per accession), **sieve** (optional: thin near-duplicates), then **msa**. The LexicMap route runs **lexicmap**, optionally **sieve**, and (for consistency with the kmindex route) optionally **msa**.
**lexicmap** already emits a reference-coordinate MSA as part of its multi-HSP tiling: every row is the reference length, with no gaps and no Ns, because the clean cohort gates (``--require-full-length``, ``--min-pident``, ``--max-internal-stops``) only let through accessions whose tiled sequence sits on the reference grid without needing an insertion. On three real cohorts (``erg11`` collapsed, ``erg11`` per-accession, SARS-CoV-2 spike collapsed; 27 to 14,594 sequences) re-running MAFFT ``--auto`` on the lexicmap output reproduced it byte-for-byte, every row and every column. The **msa** step on the LexicMap route is therefore a no-op on strict clean-cohort data and can be skipped. It still has to run on the walker route, whose per-accession reconstructions are not pre-aligned.
